note: Researched recommendations, written in the site's voice but by somebody who has not been. Opinionated on purpose — a list of facts is not a guide — but every card says plainly that it was researched rather than visited, and a handwritten note in notes.json overrules any of it. This file exists because nothing else can fill it: Wikidata holds three cafes in the whole of Bengaluru and no open dataset in India describes everyday food. See SOURCES.md.
rules: Every record needs a source and a lastVerified date. If it cannot be checked, it does not go in.
Say what to order and when to go. 'Lovely atmosphere' helps nobody.
No opening hours in prose. OpenStreetMap carries them, js/hours.js reads them, and a time written here is a time that rots.
quality and uniqueness cap at 4 here. 5 is reserved for somewhere one of you actually loved.
Always pin `match` with a zone. A chain with fourteen branches will otherwise resolve to whichever one the index happened to list first.

items.title: Vidyarthi Bhavan
items.why: Gandhi Bazaar since 1943, opened to feed students at the National College up the road — Vidyarthi Bhavan means student house. The benne masala dosa is the order and it is fried in enough butter to be a decision. Expect to give your name, wait on the pavement and share a table. Go on a weekday morning; weekends are a different and worse experience.
items.source: Wikipedia; Karnataka Tourism; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms
items.why: Started as the Brahmin Coffee Club in 1924 and in the Art Deco building on Lalbagh Road since 1959, with a walk-through kitchen that was a radical idea at the time. The rava idli was invented here during the Second World War, when rice ran short and Yagnanarayana Maiya tried semolina instead. Order that, and the filter coffee.
items.source: Wikipedia; The Better India; Citizen Matters; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Koshy's
items.why: St Mark's Road, and the room where Bengaluru has argued with itself since 1940 — journalists, academics, people nursing one coffee for two hours. The food is beside the point and the mutton cutlet is the thing to order anyway. Nobody will hurry you, which is the entire proposition.
items.source: Wikidata (restaurant in Bangalore); published coverage; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Shree Sagar CTR
items.why: Malleswaram, and the benne dose that every argument about the best in the city eventually comes back to. Small, quick, cash-friendly, and busiest at breakfast. Order the dose and a coffee and do not over-plan it.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Karavalli
items.why: Coastal Karnataka and Mangalorean cooking done seriously, in a garden courtyard off Residency Road. The appams and the fish curry are what it is for. The expensive end of the city, and the one worth it.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lalbagh Botanical Gardens
items.why: Commissioned by Hyder Ali in the 1760s and finished by Tipu Sultan, with a Victorian glasshouse modelled on the Crystal Palace at the centre of it. The rock at the south end is older than anything else in the city by a margin measured in aeons. Early morning is when Bengaluru actually uses it.
items.source: Published coverage; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Cubbon Park
items.why: Three hundred acres in the middle of the city, laid out in 1870, and closed to traffic on Sundays — which is the day to go, when it fills with runners, skaters and people reading on the grass. The bamboo grove and the rose garden are the two corners worth walking to rather than past.
items.source: Published coverage; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Champaca Bookstore, Library & Cafe
items.why: Up a flight of stairs off Edward Road: a bookshop with a lending library and a small cafe attached, curated hard rather than stocked wide — translation, writing from the south, independent presses. The kind of shelf where you leave with something you had not heard of.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blossom Book House
items.why: Church Street, three floors, second-hand and new stacked together to the ceiling with only the loosest idea of order. Budget an hour you had not planned to spend. Prices are negotiable at the top of the building and not at the bottom.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Toit
items.why: The Indiranagar brewpub that started the city's microbrewery habit, and still the busiest room on 100 Feet Road. Go for the beer brewed on the premises rather than the menu, and go early — after eight there is a wait on the stairs.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Corner House
items.why: Ice cream, and specifically the Death by Chocolate, which is less a dessert than a local institution with a queue. Nothing about it is subtle and that is the point. Best late, after dinner, which is when everyone else goes.
items.source: Published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Ulsoor Lake Park
items.why: One of the lakes the city was built around and one of the few still worth walking, with islands in the middle and boating at the north end. Bengaluru has lost most of its tanks to construction; this is what the others looked like. Early, before the heat.
items.source: Published coverage; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: City Market
items.why: Krishna Rajendra Market, and everyone calls it City Market. Built in 1921 as the New General Market and renamed in 1946 after the Maharaja whose government put it up, on a site that was a kalyani — a temple tank — attributed to Kempegowda, who founded the city. It is one of Asia's largest flower markets: over twenty tonnes a day, and fifty in wedding season. Go at six in the morning for the flowers, which is the only hour that makes sense.
items.source: Wikipedia; Something Curated; published coverage; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Malleshwaram 8th Cross Market
items.why: Malleswaram was laid out in 1898 when the plague drove people out of the old city, and 8th Cross off Sampige Road is still its busiest street — flower stalls from five in the morning, then vegetables and fruit. Sampige and Margosa Roads are named after the trees that used to line them. Come early, and eat at one of the tiffin rooms on the same stretch afterwards.
items.source: Citizen Matters; published coverage; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Iyengar's Bakery
items.why: The Iyengar bakery is Bangalore's own institution, and this is one. The first opened in Chikpet in 1898, after an Englishman taught H S Thirumalachar to bake bread; most of the founders came from a cluster of villages in Hassan district, and they turned out to be very good at it. Honey cake first, then a khara bun and a benne biscuit. Baked each afternoon for that evening and the next morning, so go late in the day.
items.source: The Quint; Slurrp; CurryLore; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Yeshwantpur Market
items.why: The wholesale market on the north-west edge, next to the APMC yard, and the one that supplies the smaller markets you will otherwise shop in. Worth the trip if you want to see the scale rather than buy at it — it is a working market and not laid on for anybody.
items.source: Published coverage; position confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Albert Bakery
items.why: Mohammed Suleman started it as a godown on Sangam Road in 1902 and it became a bakery in Frazer Town in 1921 — named Albert, probably after the prince, to bring in the Anglo-Indian trade. The mutton keema samosas and the coconut puffs, and in Ramadan the brain puff, which is the reason people cross the city that month.
items.source: Bakers Brûlée; LBB; Local Samosa; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Thom's Bakery
items.why: Frazer Town since 1970 and grown into a small supermarket around the original counter, which is still where to go. Plum cake at Christmas is what it is famous for; the puffs and the bread the rest of the year.
items.source: the bakery's listing; The Tasty Tales; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: LJ Iyengars Bakery
items.why: An Iyengar bakery in the south of the city, which is where most of them are. The tradition started in Chikpet in 1898 and the founders came from a handful of villages in Hassan district; the menu is the same one everywhere and that is the point. Honey cake, khara bun, benne biscuit. Late afternoon, when the day's baking comes out.
items.source: The Quint; Slurrp; CurryLore; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Hatti Kaapi
items.why: Filter coffee, standing up, at a price that is the argument — Lakshman Swamy started it in November 2009 to sell the city's own coffee properly and cheaply. A bar and a few stools and nothing to linger over, which is exactly how filter coffee is meant to be drunk.
items.source: Hatti Kaapi; Tripadvisor listing; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Third Wave Coffee Roasters
items.why: The first one, which opened on 24 September 2016 on 80 Feet Road after a year of the founders working out what to build. There are forty-odd across the city now and the rest are a chain; this is where Bengaluru's specialty coffee habit started.
items.source: YourStory; LBB; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dyu Art Cafe
items.area: KHB Colony, Next To Mangala Kalyana Mantapa 5th Block Adugod
items.why: An old Kerala-Portuguese bungalow in Koramangala with courtyards and gabled roofs, run as a café and a gallery at once — the owners wanted somewhere artists could show work to people who had only come for a sandwich. Sit in the courtyard, and look at the walls on the way out.
items.source: IBTimes India; LBB; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: The roaster that got Indians drinking Indian coffee as something other than instant, buying single-estate beans from Karnataka and Kerala — which in Bengaluru means from a couple of hundred kilometres away. Here for the north of the city.
items.source: Published coverage; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
items.why: Since 1965, and the menu has not changed since: idli, vada, khara bath, kesari bath, coffee. Everything comes with the coconut chutney that is the entire reason for the queue. Standing only. Go early — it is a breakfast place and it runs out.
items.source: Time Out Bangalore; LBB; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lavonne Café
items.why: The café of a pastry school — Lavonne was started in 2012 by three chefs as India's first dedicated international baking academy, and the students run the counter downstairs while the classes go on above. On a quiet street off Double Road. The croissants hold their shape and flake properly, which is the test and the reason to come.
items.source: Time Out Bengaluru; LBB; Lavonne Academy; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sharon Tea Stall
items.why: A tea stall on the corner of Thippasandra Road that sells over a thousand cups a day. Daniel was a private driver on six thousand rupees a month, leased out his house to start it, lost ten lakh on a café upstairs that failed, and kept the stall. A long board of flavoured teas, a counter of snacks, and nowhere to sit. Stand on the pavement with everybody else.
items.source: YourStory; Tripadvisor listing; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Karma Kaapi
items.why: A micro-roastery and café on 36th Cross in Jayanagar 5th Block, roasting beans from Indian estates and a few from abroad. The menu runs from filter coffee to espresso drinks; ask for whatever they roasted most recently, which is the reason to come to the roaster rather than a café.
items.source: LBB; the roaster's own site; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Go Native
items.why: Down a lane off 10th Main under a great deal of green, cooking with indigenous grains, pulses and spices — contemporary South Indian food that uses millets where you would expect rice. The menu changes; vegan dishes are marked. Lunch in the garden is the right way to do it.
items.source: HappyCow; Bindu Gopal Rao; confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kopitiam Lah
items.why: A Malaysian-Singaporean coffee shop, which Bengaluru did not have and now queues for. Order kaya toast with soft-boiled eggs and a kopi, or the nasi lemak if it is lunch. Small room, quick turnover, better alone or in pairs than as a group.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Una Hacienda
items.why: The agave bar next to Spirit Forward, from the same team: mezcal and tequila taken seriously, with small Mexican plates to keep you upright. Start here, walk ten steps, finish there.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dali & Gala
items.why: A surrealist-themed cocktail bar on Museum Road where the drinks are as theatrical as the room. Go for one or two and to look around; order whatever the bartender is proudest of.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Yauatcha
items.why: Dim sum done with the precision of the London original. Order the har gau, the crispy duck rolls and one of the macarons at the end. Lunch is the smarter visit — same dumplings, easier table.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Harima
items.why: One of the city's longest-running Japanese kitchens, izakaya in spirit: grilled skewers, sashimi, rice bowls and a proper sake list. Sit at the counter if you can.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Comal
items.why: Mexican cooking that starts from the masa rather than the cheese. Order tacos and whatever is on the comal that day, with a mezcal. A good, loud dinner.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Malgudi Mylari Mane
items.why: The Mysore Mylari dosa — small, soft, spongy, served with butter and coconut chutney — brought to Koramangala. Order a plate of two and a filter coffee. Breakfast is the time.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Monkey Bar
items.why: The gastropub that made bar food with Indian swagger a Bengaluru thing. Beer, a plate of the house snacks to share, and a noisy table of friends is exactly the use.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Bier Library
items.why: A Koramangala brewpub with its own beers on tap and food that is better than it needs to be. Order a tasting flight before committing to a pint.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Baan Phad Thai
items.why: Thai cooking that tastes like Thailand rather than a menu approximation of it. Order the curries and a som tam, and tell them you can take the heat if you can.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Only Place
items.why: A steakhouse on Museum Road since the 1960s, from when Bengaluru was still a cantonment town. Order the steak with mushroom sauce and the apple pie. Unfussy and unchanged, which is why people keep coming back.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: LUPA
items.why: Manu Chandra's big, handsome European dining room on MG Road. Pastas made in-house, a strong bar and a room that works for an occasion. Book for dinner.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Pizza 4P's
items.why: The Vietnamese-Japanese pizzeria's first Indian outpost. Order the burrata pizza — they make the cheese themselves — and one of the Asian-leaning pies to compare. Expect a wait at weekends.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: 23rd Street Pizza
items.why: New York slices on Castle Street: thin, big, foldable, by the slice or the pie. Cheap, fast and open late enough to be the end of the night.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026) and published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Shezan
items.why: An old-school Lavelle Road dining room, open since 1989, and one of the few places around here that has not been redone for Instagram. The menu is long, from Mughlai to Continental to Chinese. Stick to the Mughlai: kebabs, a curry and rotis. Lunch is the calm time.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026); shezan.in; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Dolphins
items.why: A dim, retro bar-restaurant on Wheeler Road in Cox Town. Go for Indo-Chinese with cold beer: chilli chicken, a fried rice and a table of friends. It is not trying to be anything else, and that is why people like it.
items.source: Named in a Bengaluru eat-and-drink list (varun760, Instagram, Sept 2026); Zomato; Tripadvisor; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Meghana Foods
items.why: The Andhra-style biryani Bengaluru argues about, and the Residency Road branch is the central one. Order the boneless chicken biryani and nothing else on the first visit. Expect a queue at lunch and fast, loud service once you are in.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: KOKO
items.why: The Mumbai Cantonese-Japanese restaurant's Bengaluru outpost, in Prestige Icon on Old Airport Road: several floors, a lounge bar and a room built for dressing up. Order the dim sum and the black cod, and a cocktail from the bar first.
items.source: kokorestaurants.com; LBB; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Vapour
items.why: One of the 100 Feet Road brewpubs that made Indiranagar what it is. Go for the rooftop and a pitcher of the house beer on a warm evening; the food is there to go with the beer.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Iron Hill Bengaluru
items.why: A brewery on the Outer Ring Road built to industrial scale: huge, several levels, and beer brewed on site. Come with a group after work and start with a tasting paddle.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sarjapura Social
items.why: Social's Sarjapur Road outpost: a big, loud café-bar that works as an office by day and a bar by night. Cheap cocktails in jars, bar food, and no one minding the noise.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Roxie
items.why: A 35,000-square-foot Italian mansion on Haralur Road, built to look like the Amalfi Coast: a courtyard, bougainvillea, a stone bar and a bakery at the door. Order cocktails and small plates, and go at sunset when the courtyard is at its best.
items.source: Homegrown; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Biergarten Brewery & Kitchen
items.why: A German-style beer garden with house-brewed wheat beers and lagers and a big open-air deck, handy for the Outer Ring Road crowd after work. Order the hefeweizen and a plate of sausages, and sit outside.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Arbor Brewing Company
items.why: The Bengaluru branch of the Michigan brewery, on Magrath Road, and one of the city's first brewpubs. The beers are more varied than most — Belgians and sours sit next to the pale ales — so order a flight.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Araku Coffee
items.why: The café from the Araku Valley coffee co-operative, where tribal farmers in the Eastern Ghats grow the beans. Order a pour-over of a single-estate lot and compare it with the espresso. It is a calm, bright room for a weekday morning.
items.source: arakucoffee.in; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: 6oz Coffee and Roasters
items.why: A small Ulsoor roaster-café where the coffee is the point. Ask what they are roasting this week and have it as a filter or a flat white. Better for one or two people than for a group.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Coffee Mechanics
items.why: The Hennur branch of a local specialty chain, with a long menu of brew methods and cold coffees. A good neighbourhood spot to work from on a slow afternoon.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Milano Ice Cream
items.why: Italian-style gelato made in small batches, and one of the city's go-to scoops. Try the seasonal fruit flavours next to a dark chocolate. Best after dinner on a warm night, when there is a queue out the door.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: LICK - Lavonne Ice Cream Kitchen
items.why: The ice-cream counter from the Lavonne pastry school, so the flavours come with a pastry chef's precision. Order whatever is newest, and pair it with a pastry from Lavonne round the corner.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Glen's Bakehouse
items.why: The 100 Feet Road bakery-café where half of Indiranagar has had a birthday cake. Order the red velvet, or a slice of something from the counter with a coffee. Afternoons are its best time.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sour House
items.why: A Koramangala bakery built around sourdough, with a long ferment and a crackling crust. Buy a loaf to take home, and have a sandwich or a morning bun while you are there. Go early, before the bread sells out.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Krumb Kraft
items.why: A small bakery off Old Airport Road with a proper case of croissants, laminated pastries and tarts. Order whatever came out of the oven last. Mornings are best.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Amintiri
items.why: An HSR Layout patisserie making European-style entremets and tarts that look almost too neat to cut into. Order a plated dessert with coffee, and take a box home.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Zed The Baker
items.why: A bakery-café on Palace Road with a serious bread and viennoiserie counter. Order the croissants or a sandwich on their sourdough, and buy a loaf on the way out.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Rolling Pin
items.why: An Indiranagar patisserie known for its cakes and dessert jars. Come for a slice of cake in the afternoon, or order a whole one ahead for an occasion.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mirth
items.why: A 65-seat cocktail bar on 100 Feet Road, dim and red-lit, with Pan-Asian food that holds up to the drinks. The bar's own advice is to start light and finish strong: begin with something fizzy and fruity, and end on something bold.
items.source: Outlook Traveller; Restaurant India; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Travellers Bungalow
items.why: Made up to look like an old colonial rest-house — a wooden ceiling, vintage Crompton fans, patterned wallpaper — on 12th Main. The gin cocktails are the draw. The food wanders the world, from khinkali to paella, so order a few small plates to share.
items.source: Zee Zest; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Chianti
items.why: The first and smallest Chianti, open in Koramangala 5th Block since 2012 and hardly changed since. The pasta is handmade, and there is a monthly special. Order the pasta over the pizza. It is a small room, so book at weekends.
items.source: Brinda S Narayan; Resy; Tripadvisor; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Smoke House Deli
items.why: The Lavelle Road branch of the all-day European deli, in a bright white room made for a long brunch. Go for weekend brunch, and order the eggs and one of the sandwiches.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Amicii
items.why: A two-floor pub on 100 Feet Road with a rooftop under a retractable roof, so rain does not cancel the evening. The menu is global comfort food and cocktails, and the calendar runs from karaoke to retro nights. Check what is on before you go.
items.source: Restaurant India; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Phurr
items.why: Vegetarian fine dining, and arguably the city's most talked-about. Inventive Indian-fusion plates and mocktails in place of a bar. Take the tasting route, and bring the friend who says vegetarian food is never the main event.
items.source: phurr.co.in; Swiggy Dineout; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nuage Pâtisserie & Café
items.why: A small Indiranagar patisserie-café for French-style pastries and cakes. Order a pastry and a coffee in the afternoon, and take something home in a box.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Hole In The Wall Cafe

match.name: The Hole In The Wall Cafe

items.why: Koramangala's breakfast place since 2009. It started as a 25-seat garage and grew into a villa-like café in a 4th Block lane. It opens at eight. Order the pancakes or waffles, or one of the big breakfast platters, and come on a weekday — weekend mornings mean a queue.
items.source: theholeinthewallcafe.org; LBB; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Truffles
items.why: The Koramangala burger place every student in the city has queued for. American-style burgers, thick shakes and noise. Go on a weekday afternoon, between three and five, to skip the wait.
items.source: LBB; Tripadvisor; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Roastea
items.why: A bungalow café on 80 Feet Road with a garden to sit in, coffee and tea from its own roasting, and vegetarian food. Order a bagel or the handkerchief pasta. It is a good place to work from for a morning.
items.source: roastea.in; LBB; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nasi and Mee
items.why: A long-running Koramangala spot for Malaysian and Singaporean food. Order the nasi lemak, a char kway teow and the Hainanese chicken rice, and share them.
items.source: Tripadvisor; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Daily Sushi
items.why: A casual sushi bar that made maki an everyday lunch in Bengaluru rather than an occasion. Order a couple of rolls and a bowl. Quick, reliable, and priced for a weekday.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Reservoire
items.why: A multi-level cocktail bar on 17th Main that claims to be India's largest, with a menu of more than two hundred cocktails and a rooftop under a retractable roof. Come with a group and work your way down the list.
items.source: thereservoire.com; LBB; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Koramangala Social
items.why: The Social chain's Koramangala outpost: a café-bar that is a place to work by day and a loud, cheap bar by night. Cocktails come in jars, the food is made to share, and nobody minds the noise.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Old Madras Baking Company
items.why: A bakery on St Mark's Road with a proper counter of breads, pastries and cakes, and a café to eat them in. Order a croissant and a coffee in the morning, and take a loaf home.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Kind
items.why: The Kind Roastery & Brew Room: specialty coffee roasted on site, and a menu that looks after vegan and gluten-free diets without making a fuss about it. Ask what is on the brew bar this week and have it as a pour-over.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lucky Chan
items.why: A lively, neon-lit pan-Asian bar-restaurant. Order dim sum and a bowl of noodles to share, with a cocktail. It is a loud dinner with friends rather than a quiet one.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Pizza Bakery
items.why: Wood-fired, thin-crust pizza from a local chain that takes its dough seriously. Order one of the classic pies and a salad. An easy, dependable weeknight dinner.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kampot
items.why: A pan-Asian restaurant named after the Cambodian pepper town, cooking Vietnamese and Cambodian dishes alongside the dim sum. Order something Khmer, and finish with the mango sticky rice.
items.source: Zomato; EazyDiner; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Radio Bar
items.why: The Mumbai bar's first Bengaluru outpost. The walls are covered in cassettes and CDs, there is live music or a DJ most nights, and the drinks are classic cocktails and craft beer. Come for the retro soundtrack and a big table of friends.
items.source: Hospibuz; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bellandur Social
items.why: The Social chain's Outer Ring Road outpost: a place to work from by day and a loud, cheap bar by night, full of the tech parks around it. Cocktails come in jars and the plates are made to share.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Biergarten Brewery & Kitchen
items.why: A German-style beer garden in Koramangala, with house-brewed wheat beers and lagers and a big open-air deck. Order the hefeweizen and a plate of sausages, and sit outside.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Hard Rock Cafe
items.why: The St Mark's Road Hard Rock: a big, loud room of rock memorabilia, with live bands on many nights. You know what it is. Go for a gig night, a burger and a pitcher, and do not expect anything quiet.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Hard Rock Cafe
items.why: The Whitefield Hard Rock, closer to the tech parks: the same memorabilia, burgers and live music as the city-centre one, for an after-work night out on the east side.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Oota Bangalore
items.why: Karnataka on one menu, from the Windmills team near ITPL. The dishes travel the state: Mangalore buns and ghee roast from the coast, Maddur vade from the south, donne biryani, and food from the Western Ghats and the north. Order across regions and share everything. The bar pours Windmills' own beer.
items.source: LBB; Tripadvisor; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lavonne
items.why: The Whitefield outpost of the Lavonne pastry school's café. Slow-fermented sourdough and croissants that flake properly — the laminated ham-and-cheese is the one to order. Go in the morning, and take a loaf home.
items.source: Lavonne; MyReserveTable; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Farmhouse Kitchen & Bakery
items.why: A bakery-kitchen on a farm off Varthur Road, which is as close to the countryside as Whitefield gets. Go for a slow weekend breakfast outdoors, and buy bread on the way out.
items.source: The Vine Bangalore; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lakeview Milk Bar
items.why: The Whitefield branch of the MG Road milk bar that has been making sundaes and thick shakes since 1930. The same menu as the original, without the drive into town.
items.source: lakeviewmilkbar.in; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Corner House
items.why: The east-side branch of Bengaluru's own ice-cream parlour. Order the Death by Chocolate, which is what everyone orders. Best late, after dinner.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: The Whitefield branch of the Delhi roaster that buys directly from Indian estates. Order a pour-over of whichever single estate they are featuring, or a cold brew on a hot afternoon. A reliable place to work from.
items.source: bluetokaicoffee.com; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Veena Stores
items.why: A standing-only breakfast counter on 15th Cross that began as a condiments shop and has been serving since 1977. Order the idli-vada with the thin green chutney, which is unlimited and the reason people come. Eat on the pavement, early.
items.source: Karnataka Tourism; Finely Chopped; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Hotel Janatha
items.why: A Malleshwaram dosa house going since the 1970s, a few doors from the 8th Cross market. The butter masala dosa comes with a smear of red chutney inside, which is Janatha's own. Quieter than CTR, and many locals prefer it.
items.source: LBB; MetroSaga; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Hallimane
items.why: A big, busy self-service vegetarian place built to look like a village house, with Karnataka food at canteen prices. Order the akki rotti and a Mysore-style meal, and pay at the counter first. It is a favourite with IISc students.
items.source: IISc student guides; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Corner House
items.why: The New BEL Road branch of Bengaluru's own ice-cream parlour, a short walk from the IISc gates. Order the Death by Chocolate, which is what everyone orders.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Glen's Bakehouse
items.why: The New BEL Road branch of the bakery-café, close to IISc: red velvet, cakes by the slice and a coffee. An easy afternoon stop.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Truffles
items.why: The New BEL Road branch of the burger place Bengaluru's students have queued for since the Koramangala original. American-style burgers and thick shakes, cheap and loud.
items.source: LBB; Tripadvisor; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Kind Roastery and Brewroom
items.why: The JP Nagar Kind, a short ride from IIM: specialty coffee roasted in-house, and a menu that looks after vegan and gluten-free eaters. Ask what is on the brew bar and have it as a pour-over.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Glen's Bakehouse
items.why: The Glen's closest to IIM Bangalore, off Bannerghatta Road. Cakes by the slice, red velvet and a coffee — the standard escape from campus for an afternoon.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nagarjuna
items.why: Andhra meals on a banana leaf, from the Residency Road institution. It is refilled until you stop them. Order the meal with the chicken or mutton fry, and have the gunpowder with ghee on the rice. About a kilometre from IIM.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Corner House
items.why: The Corner House nearest IIM Bangalore, for the Death by Chocolate after dinner.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: URU Brewpark
items.why: A brewery set in a park on Bannerghatta Road: one and a half acres, with a container bar, a bistro, a café and a gin garden where you build your own gin cocktail. It is pet-friendly and best in daylight, so go for a long weekend afternoon.
items.source: urubrewpark.in; LBB; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Beku
items.why: A café, bakery and bookshop in one — beku means 'I want' in Kannada. Order an eggless croissant and the white chocolate and rose latte, then browse the shelves. Good for working from, and there are events in the evenings.
items.source: Zomato; Bangalore Eats; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Diha
items.why: A specialty coffee bar by day and a wine bar by night, with wood-fired pizza. Come for single-origin coffee in the afternoon, or for a pizza and a glass of something from the short boutique wine list.
items.source: diha.cafe; Curly Tales; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: 154 Breakfast Club
items.why: An all-day breakfast place: pancakes, eggs any way, and waffles, served whenever you happen to wake up. Go for a late weekend breakfast.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Rameshwaram Cafe
items.why: The JP Nagar branch of the darshini that turned ghee podi idli and a crisp ghee dosa into a queue at every hour of the day. Order at the counter, eat standing, and have a filter coffee to finish.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bengaluru Cafe
items.why: A Jayanagar 2nd Block breakfast counter where the butter masala dosa is made in front of you and costs almost nothing. Idli and uppittu are just as good. Go early.
items.source: Tripadvisor; magicpin; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Basaveshwar Khanavali
items.why: North Karnataka meals in Jayanagar: jolada rotti (jowar flatbread), ennegai brinjal, pulses and chutney powders on a plate that keeps being refilled. Go for lunch, and come hungry.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Taaza Thindi
items.why: A tiny, stand-and-eat Jayanagar darshini with a short menu and a long queue. Order the masala dosa and a vada, then a coffee. It is fast, cheap and good.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: The Jayanagar Blue Tokai on 10th Main. Order a pour-over of whichever single estate they are featuring, or a cold brew on a hot afternoon. A dependable place to work from.
items.source: bluetokaicoffee.com; Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Iris Cafe and Kitchen
items.why: A JP Nagar café-kitchen with a relaxed room and a menu for brunch and long lunches. Go on a weekend late morning.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Silaa - The Garden Cafe
items.why: A café in a garden in Malleshwaram, with tables under the trees, which is exactly the point. Come for a slow breakfast or a long coffee in the afternoon, and sit outside.

items.title: Third Wave Coffee Roasters
items.why: The Sadashivanagar Third Wave, a short ride from IISc: a reliable flat white or pour-over, and plenty of tables to work from.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Smoor
items.why: The Sadashivanagar Smoor, for chocolate desserts, cakes and a hot chocolate. Order one of the chocolate tarts. It is an easy dessert stop close to IISc.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: 1522 - The Pub
items.why: A no-frills, budget pub near New BEL Road that IISc students have used for years. Cheap beer, bar snacks and a crowded room. You go for the company, not the décor.

items.title: Corner House
items.why: The Corner House nearest Christ University, for the Death by Chocolate after class.
items.source: Zomato; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Shiro
items.why: UB City's big, dramatic Asian room: a high ceiling, giant statues, and sushi and pan-Asian plates. It is a place for an occasion or a date. Order the sushi and a cocktail, and sit on the terrace if the weather allows.

items.title: Toscano
items.why: Reliable Tuscan-leaning Italian in UB City, with pastas, thin-crust pizzas and a good tiramisu. A safe choice for a group that cannot agree, and the terrace is pleasant at lunch.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Sanchez
items.why: A Mexican cantina in UB City. Order tacos and a margarita, and sit outside on a warm evening.
items.source: LBB; Slurrp; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Farzi Cafe
items.why: Zorawar Kalra's modern Indian café, where familiar dishes come with a twist and a bit of theatre on the plate. Order a few small plates to share, and one of the cocktails. It is loud and fun rather than serious.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Laduree
items.why: The Paris macaron house, in UB City. Buy a box of macarons — rose and salted caramel are the classics — and have a tea and a pastry in the salon if you have time.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Cafe Noir
items.why: A French-style café-bistro in UB City for croissants, quiche, crêpes and a proper coffee. A good brunch before a walk in Cubbon Park next door.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Skyye
items.why: A rooftop bar at the top of UB City, with the city spread out around you. Come for a drink at sunset, before it turns into a club later in the night.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Biere Club
items.why: Bengaluru's first microbrewery, open since 2009 just off UB City. It is where the city's craft-beer habit began. Order a taster of the house beers and some bar food to go with them.
items.source: Zomato; published coverage; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap
